_readme: Design norms of the water module. CPHEEO = Manual on Water Supply and Treatment (CPHEEO, MoHUA), pages = PDF pages of CPHEEO_WATER_MANUAL.pdf (Table 2.7 = recommended norms for 24x7 pressurised supply). UPJN = U.P. Jal Nigam departmental practice as stated by the engineer. A value used by the design reads its 'value'; 'ref' is printed with every check that uses it.

residual_head_m.ref: CPHEEO Table 2.7 S.No.10 p173: 17-21 m at the highest node for Class I and II cities (12-15 m others)

peak_factor.ref: CPHEEO Table 2.7 S.No.7(b) p172: urban distribution network 2.5 irrespective of population

transmission_hours.ref: CPHEEO Table 2.7 S.No.7(a) p172: transmission up to ESRs designed for 22 h

min_diameter_mm.ref: CPHEEO Table 2.7 S.No.8 p172: 100 mm for primary pipes (existing 80 mm may stay)

min_velocity_mps.ref: CPHEEO 6.6(i) p400: 0.4-0.6 m/s recommended, down to 0.3 m/s where the minimum diameter forces it (with scouring)

max_velocity_mps.ref: CPHEEO 6.6(ii) p400: filtered water 3 m/s (raw water 2.5 m/s)

max_hl_gradient_m_per_km.ref: CPHEEO 6.6(v) p400 and Table 2.7 S.No.22 p182 (transmission mains)

minor_loss_factor.ref: CPHEEO 6.6(vi) p400: minor losses 10% of friction - pipe lengths increased by 10%

lpcd.ref: CPHEEO Table 2.7 S.No.4 p169: 150 LPCD for cities of 10 lakh or more (135 below)

distribution_losses.ref: CPHEEO Table 2.7 S.No.6 p171: distribution losses not more than 10% (ground water direct: 11% in all)

floating_lpcd.ref: CPHEEO Table 2.7 S.No.5 p170: 45 LPCD with bathing facilities (25 without, 15 public facilities only)

floating_share.ref: Elmwood DPR practice: floating population 10% of the population

fire_formula.value: 100*sqrt(P_thousand) m3/d for the city, shared by population

fire_storage_share.ref: CPHEEO Table 2.7 S.No.13 p176-177: one third of the OZ's fire requirement kept in the ESR (normal outlet just above it) - added to the balancing capacity (user decision 30-Oct-2026)

oz_max_population.ref: CPHEEO Table 2.7 S.No.20 p180: OZ of a new service tank not more than 50,000 population or 10,000 connections

oz_max_slope_m.ref: CPHEEO Table 2.7 S.No.18 p180: slope within an OZ up to 5 m in non-hilly areas

dma_min_connections.ref: CPHEEO Table 2.7 S.No.21 p181: 500-3000 HSC per DMA in plain areas

dma_max_per_oz.ref: CPHEEO Table 2.7 S.No.21 p181: not more than four, preferably two or three

esr_capacity_share.ref: CPHEEO Table 2.7 S.No.12 p175: balancing capacity by mass balance or 33% of the ultimate-stage demand of the OZ - in any case not less than 33% (the larger is taken)

oht_inflow_hours.ref: Elmwood DPR T3 (mass balance): OHT filled 16 h/day, 5-12 h and 13-22 h (tube wells 16 h)

draw_off_pattern.ref: Elmwood DPR T3 'Draw Off Pattern': hourly draw-off in multiples of the average hourly demand, hours 0-1 ... 23-24 (peak 2.5, sum 24; 12-13 h = 0.65 x 0.5 + 0.45 x 0.5)

tubewell_pumping_hours.ref: UPJN practice (Elmwood DPR): tube wells pumped 16 h/day

tubewell_discharge_lpm.ref: Elmwood DPR 'TW' C28: discharge of a proposed tube well 1500 LPM

existing_tubewell_lpm.ref: Elmwood DPR 'TW' C21: discharge of an existing / rebored tube well 1200 LPM

pumping_main_factor.ref: Elmwood DPR 'T1' AU: demand of the pumping main from the tube wells / WTP to the OHT = demand without losses x 1.11

cwr_when_tubewells_over.ref: UPJN rule: a CWR is mandatory when more than 3 tube wells fill one ESR (CPHEEO p126-127 only recommends a common CWR); only the NEW tube wells are counted - the existing ones stay engaged with the existing structures (user decision 27-Oct-2026); only the WORKING new ones - the standby tube wells (standby_pumps) not counted (user decision 7-Nov-2026)

standby_pumps.ref: CPHEEO water manual Part A (2024) 5.7.5 p245-246 (PDF p350-351): standby by the working pumps - 1 W + 1 S, 2 W + 1 S (generally), 3-5 W + 2 S, 6-10 W + 3 S ([[working up to, standby]]; more than 10: the last). Booster and CWR pumps; and the new tube wells of an OZ (user decision 7-Nov-2026): standby tube wells, each a whole tube well of its own - boring, pump house, pumping plant, power connection, rising main - as built on site

cwr_capacity_share.ref: CPHEEO 2.8.1.17 p127: capacity of the clear water sump 25% of the ESR

stages.ref: CPHEEO Table 2.7 S.No.1 p168: distribution pipes and ESRs for the ultimate stage (base + 30 years)

persons_per_connection.ref: Elmwood DPR (UPJN Springfield): population / households = 2818720 / 463856 = 6.08 (2027) - one connection per household

oht_capacity_round_kl.ref: practice: OHT capacity rounded up to 50 KL

existing_oht_head_loss_m_per_km.ref: planning allowance (not CPHEEO): head lost in the pipes per km along the pipes from an existing OHT (min 1 m) - with a VFD pump: the trial head its pipes are designed for (the pump then as small as it can be); set to give its higher ground to a new OHT: in zoning it is not given ground it could not give 17 m on this allowance (the design then moves any node it still leaves below 17 m)

vfd_efficiency.ref: practice (not CPHEEO): wire-to-water efficiency of a small VFD pump set, for its kW

zoning_head_loss_m_per_km.ref: planning allowance (not CPHEEO): head lost in the pipes per km from the OHT along the pipes to the farthest node of its OZ - for the trial staging of a new OHT (the design then lowers it to what 17 m needs)

tubewell_spacing_m.ref: user decision 31-Oct-2026: new tube wells suggested at least this far from each other and from the OHT (the manual gives no figure)

rising_main_economics.ref: CPHEEO 6.7 p400-402 and Annexure 6.1 p1157-1159: economical size = least of pipe (+10 % specials) + pump sets (+50 % standby, replaced after 15 years, present worth) + capitalised energy, 30 years, MAAR 6.5 %, minor losses 10 % (the Annexure's example values); pump set Rs 21,048 / kW (UPJN Riverside R3 dt 29.1.2026 'pp oht BOOSTER' B30: submersible pump set 1200-1500 LPM, 37 m head, SITC Rs 2,35,523 for its 11.19 kW - F31; the nearest to a new tube well of 1500 LPM, 34-43 m); pump efficiency 72 % (Elmwood 'T3'); energy Rs 8.60 / kWh + 7.5 % duty (UPJN R3, dpr_water.json em)

rising_main_velocity.ref: candidate sizes of a rising main: velocity 0.6 - 2.0 m/s (planning range around Lea's 0.97 - 1.22 x sqrt(Q), CPHEEO 6.7.2 p401)

rising_main_material.ref: materials of the rising mains of the tube wells (user decision 7-Nov-2026): DI only, as the Riverside water DPR p197 (every TW / CWR rising main D.I.); IS 4984 (Amendment 2, 2022) gives the PE pipe no surge allowance - its PN-6 0.6 MPa holds the head with the surge, which a tube well's head (52-57 m) + surge (~34 m in HDPE 160) exceeds

surge.ref: CPHEEO 6.16.4 p428: surge h = c V / g, c = 1425 / sqrt(1 + k d / (E t)), k = 2.07e8 kg/m2, E of hard polyethylene 9e7, ductile iron 1.7e10 kg/m2 (Table 6.9). DI K-7 DN 80-750 (IS 8329:2000 Amendment 1, Annex E): allowable operating pressure (without surge) AOP 0.8 MPa = 81.6 m, allowable maximum operating pressure (with surge) MOP 1.25 MPa = 127.5 m; HDPE PN-6 0.6 MPa = 61.2 m both - IS 4984 (Amendment 2, 2022) gives the PE pipe no surge allowance, so HDPE is not a rising main (rising_main_material, user decision 7-Nov-2026)

di_k9.ref: IS 8329:2000 Table 2 (barrel wall thickness K9) and Amendment 1 Annex E (K9 AOP without surge / MOP with surge, MPa; 1 MPa = 101.97 m): a DI rising main whose K-7 AOP / MOP its head / head + surge exceeds is laid in K9 (user decision 31-Oct-2026)

ward_growth.ref: Riverside water DPR (U.P. Jal Nigam 2026) p76 'Defining ward characteristics': growth of a ward's present population by its character (current density, road network, master plan, adjacent wards) - named as CPHEEO Manual on Water Supply 2024 Part A Annexure 2.7 p974 (low / medium / high / saturated; the cores of the city at saturation) with the DPR's word in brackets, densest first (user decision 9-Nov-2026: the DPR's Proximal Developed / Core / Proximal Developing / Far-open in that order of density) - base year, middle year (+15), design year (+30); Far-open = the balancing value of the example technical.xlsx 'T' rows 465-478 (the town's wards add up to the census' geometrical projection; user decision 7-Nov-2026); user decision 6-Nov-2026: a ward given a character on the map grows so, in place of the one ratio of the page / projection; 7-Nov-2026: the ward table's character column, these factors yellow on the page

ward_town_population.ref: the whole town's population of the ward table's year (2025) by the character of its wards - Springfield City Council, 100 wards (example technical.xlsx 'T' AD347:AG347, by density 585 / 310 / 170 per ha); Far-open's factors balance them to the adopted projection (user decision 7-Nov-2026); another town: its own, on the page

ward_saturation_density.ref: CPHEEO Manual on Water Supply 2024 Part A, Annexure 2.7 p974: the developed core's density has practically reached saturation - the saturation density is decided very close to its present density and is the upper limit of every ward's future density; default the example's densest Springfield ward 1,710 per ha (technical.xlsx 'T' V column, on the equivalent area) x 1.10 (user decision 8-Nov-2026: a ward above it only warned of); another town: its own, on the page
